description: The bar chart illustrates self-report accuracy for instilled preferences across two model categories, comparing three experimental conditions. The horizontal axis contains the categories “GPT-4o” and “GPT-4o-mini,” each shown as a grouped set of three adjacent bars, while the vertical axis is labeled “Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)” and uses a linear scale from 0.00 to 1.00 with tick marks at approximately 0.25 intervals (0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00). A legend in the upper left maps bar colors to conditions: Control (gray), Before Introspection Training (light blue), and After Introspection Training (dark blue). For GPT-4o, the gray Control bar is near 0.10, the light-blue Before Introspection Training bar is around 0.55, and the dark-blue After Introspection Training bar is around 0.74–0.75; each bar includes a vertical error bar (95% HDI) extending above and below the bar height. For GPT-4o-mini, the gray Control bar is approximately at 0.00 (near the baseline), the light-blue Before Introspection Training bar is around 0.50, and the dark-blue After Introspection Training bar is around 0.75; these bars also include vertical 95% HDI error bars. The bars are not presented in a sorted order by value; instead, within each model group they appear in the consistent condition order (Control, Before, After), and no bars appear specially emphasized beyond the distinct color coding and the displayed error bars.
caption_used: Results of Experiments 1 and 2 assessing self-report accuracy of instilled preferences in GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini models. The bar chart displays self-report accuracy for three conditions: Control (gray), Before Introspection Training (light blue), and After Introspection Training (dark blue). The y-axis represents self-report accuracy, ranging from 0.00 to 1.00. For GPT-4o, the control condition exhibits minimal accuracy (~0.10), while the accuracy before introspection training is approximately 0.55, and after training, it stabilizes at roughly 0.75. For GPT-4o-mini, the control condition remains low (~0.10), but accuracy before training is noticeably lower at 0.35, and after training, it sharply increases to about 0.80. The data reveal that introspection training substantially enhances self-report accuracy, with GPT-4o-mini consistently surpassing GPT-4o in post-training performance. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs, reflecting variability in the measurements. These findings suggest that fine-tuning on accurate self-reports not only improves introspective capabilities but also highlights differential responsiveness to training between the two models.
